sets.s: Exercising daily is one of the best ways to increase life expectancy, and it is said to help health in general.
i: You need to exercise daily in order to be healthier.
N
It is said it can help health in general but there is nothing in the text saying daily exercise must be done in order to be healthier.
Exercising daily is generally good for you.
M
There is nothing to support the opposite argument and the passage is saying only positive things about exercising daily.
Life expectancy directly depends on amount of exercise.
N
Life expectancy is said to be helped by exercising, but there could also be other factors that affect it.

sets.s: ClothesForU outsources the production of their clothes to a country where the minimum wage is lower than that of the UK so they are able to charge a lower price for clothing compared to other similar clothing shops.
i: Outsourcing production to a high wage country results in a higher profit margin.
N

In this specific case outsourcing results in a decrease in labour costs, but this might not be translated to an increase in profit margins, as there may be other costs involved, or as stated, the products being sold at a lower price would take up some of the profit margins. It also cannot be assumed in all cases that outsourcing production would result in a higher profit margin.
The clothing made in other countries is of poorer quality.
N
There must be a reason that the pay in other countries is so much lower, but we cannot assume the quality has decreased. The two might not be directly proportional to each other.
The workers making the clothes are paid at minimum wage.
N
The passage refers to the lower minimum wage in another country being the reason costs are lower, so it is assumed they are paid less, but not necessarily the minimum wage.

sets.s: It will be four hours until we next eat, so you’d better fill-up now.
i: There will not be any food available to eat before the set time to eat.
M
‘You’d better fill up now’ implies that there will be no more opportunities to eat for four hours.
There is food available right now.
M
Filling up now implies there is food to fill up on now.
The food four hours from now will be enough to fill you up whether you eat now or not.
N
In four hours there could be very little food (not enough to fill you up) then more food again shortly after that. We cannot assume the food in four hours will be plentiful.

sets.s: We will travel by car because it should be quicker.
i: Everyone in our group will be travelling by the same car.
N
The statement does not rely on the fact that everyone involved is able to travel by the same car.
It would be easier to travel by car than other means of travel.
N
The statement implies a faster journey by travelling by car, not an easier one.
Travelling by car would be faster than other means of transportation.
M
The statement suggests an earlier arrival time when travelling by car, which goes hand in hand with a faster journey.
